chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Ubaydi, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding a man: Is it permissible for him to recite the Tashahhud, the words in bowing (Ruku'), and prostration (Sujood), and the Qunut aloud? He said: 'If he wishes, he recites aloud; and if he wishes, he does not recite aloud.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And when he gives the Taslim, he raises his hands towards his face until he says 'Allahu Akbar'; and when the disc falls.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud (testimony of faith recited in prayer)
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: The Sheikh (referring to the compiler, likely Shaykh al-Tusi)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the Tashahhud and Tasbih of Ruku/Sujood aloud during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic flexibility (ikhtiyar) in the audibility of recitation during the Tashahhud, Ruku', Sujood, and Qunut, reflecting the Shia view that these acts are not strictly bound to silence or loudness. The accompanying note from the Shaykh regarding raising hands until the 'disc' (likely referring to the head or a specific gesture) falls highlights the physical etiquette (adab) accompanying these recitations, emphasizing the holistic nature of the prayer ritual.
